Hey Sam / Aisha — thanks again for the 30-minute discovery earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- What we heard: Finovo is planning to add conversational summarization and authorization checks to your payments flow; expected peak traffic around payment settlement windows. You care most about p50 latency and predictable cost.
- Next step I'd like to schedule: a dedicated capacity-sizing + technical deep dive where we bring a runtime engineer to map throughput/latency to pool size and quantization profiles.

Proposed windows (PT) — please pick one or suggest alternatives:
- Tue Jun 2, 10:00–11:00
- Wed Jun 3, 13:00–14:00

Prep items (simple):
1) Fill the attached capacity template with your peak/average QPS, avg/95th token lengths, and concurrency targets.
2) Invite any infra/neoops folks (networking, VPC) if you want VPC/private deployment questions covered.

Attaching a one-page capacity template to make the numbers quick. I’ve cc'd Marissa (SE) who will run the sizing portion.

If those times don't work, I can open more slots next week.

Thanks,

Ben — thanks for the summary and for sending the template. Wed Jun 3 13:00 PT works for us. I added Marcus (infra) to this thread so he can join the sizing call.

Quick answers for the template so you have a head start:
- Peak QPS: ~250 requests/sec during settlement spikes (we observe these ~3x/day).
- Typical sustained QPS: 30–40 req/sec.
- Average token length per request: ~450 tokens; 95th ~1200 tokens (we have long receipts sometimes).
- Longest acceptable p50 latency: 150ms; p95 < 400ms would be ideal.
- We plan to run in a customer VPC with private deployment for PCI scope.

Let me know if you need exported logs or a sample payload prior to the call. See you on Wed.

—Sam
